Addendum: Historical Note
Documentation recovered from Foundation raids on the dental laboratory of Dr. Rasmin Yelkov implicate SCP-478 as a primary source of the phenomenon observed in SCP-1994. Investigation into Dr. Yelkov's ability to communicate and capture instances of SCP-478 is ongoing.

item.title: Suggestions
item.content:encoded:
I was hoping that this thing would be more realistic. While it is easier to say "oh, it doesn't need to eat or breathe or yadda yadda," it takes away from the effect. Mystery can be good, but this one has too much. My opinion is that this article needs some more details to connect it with the idea of parasites.

Suggestion: make SCP-478 need something from humans in order to survive. Is this how it gets food? Is it part of a reproductive cycle? What does it gain from making the victim grow lots of teeth?

SCP-478 clearly affects the nervous system (and whatever biological system of which teeth are a part). I'm thinking that the chemical that it releases that triggers tooth growth is its waste, or necessary for reproduction.

Here's an idea: SCP-478 enters a person as a larva, and as it transforms into a butterfly or moth it secretes the chemical.

One final question: Does the victim still grow teeth after SCP-478 has been removed?

item.content:encoded:
The teeth grow in the stomach. The teeth have enamel, which is very resistant to acid corrosion. Due to this, the teeth are indigestible. When indigestible food is in the stomach, the stomach tries to send them to the excretory system. Provided that some of the teeth are submerged in the acid, and not all of them are on the walls, that means that in conjunction with suffering excruciating pain due to teeth being melted inside your stomach, nearly suffocating due to the presence of teeth in your lungs and throat, feeling teeth grow inside of your own skin, you'd also be hunched over a toilet, shitting out teeth.
God, I love this SCP. The more you think about it, the squickier it gets.

OK, the article is good, but the comments have forced me to make it a personal rule to read the comments on EVERY SCP. This keeps getting creepier the more I think about it, but thanks to photosynthetic's comments, now I'm going analytical with my squick…
What would it feel like? Obviously teeth in the stomach would hurt when the acid got to the nerve, but where would the brain register that nerve as being located (being as it is like a computer's new peripheral device)?
Also, stomach lining is specifically grown to contain and resist digestive acids. If part of that lining turned into gum and tooth-nerve, wouldn't severe ulceration and resultant death occur as soon as the acid at through?
Not things that need addressing, obviously, but fun (and/or creepy) to ponder.

Yeah, Bone Hive and Soft Death don't get to me so much. I think the key to body horror is to both have something that a person could imagine the feeling of, while not making it generic horror filler, i.e. biting your head off, removal of limbs, etc.

I've personally never had an organism of ambiguous identity burrow into me and turn me into pillows, and I have trouble imagining what that feels like. Same for the bone hive. On the other hand, I get tooth pains fairly frequently, and even now I can imagine getting those everywhere, and cavities in my stomach. Eugh.

With regards to A):

After recovery, they are to be kept in specialized vacuum-sealed lockers within Bio-Site 16. Instances of SCP-478 do not seem to be able to pass through solid matter, and thus may be held indefinitely unless damaged.

Extracted instances of SCP-478 do not seem to need to eat, sleep, breathe, or breed.

They're literally kept in boxes, and it's stated that once put in said boxes, no further interaction is necessary. I'm not saying this makes them "safe" by any means, but it does mean they're not too difficult to contain.

As far as B) goes:

This growth process will begin at a rate roughly twice as fast as normal tooth growth, and quickly increase in speed and severity.

They don't kill particularly fast; people are going to notice rather quickly when new teeth begin to erupt from the roof of their mouths and seek treatment.
